body:
The latest H512 submission lost quality and took longer than TL3. This cycle tests whether saved checkpoint averaging or causal representations improve complete endpoints within 30 local GPU-hours plus verified free Kaggle. B300 and paid compute remain deferred.

The six-fit i1 screen is complete: the fixed 90% baseline / 10% history blend improves F0/1001 by +0.00035953 and F2/1002 by +0.00027145, an unweighted mean paired gain of +0.00031549. Both targets improve in each cell, but history alone loses in both. Conditional component intervals are [-0.00001187,+0.00070893] and [+0.00008223,+0.00043398]; all folds are exposed and fold/seed effects cannot be separated. A masked-i1 blend also helps F2, so complementarity does not establish a history-specific mechanism. Independent source/evidence review supports a bounded strong-parent test, not production promotion.

Saved-artifact recovery is complete without new fits. The fixed projected trajectory mean adds only +0.00001096 to the existing oldZ4/WMSE blend on F0. Recovered Kaggle B16 CP5 and SWA blends both lose about 0.000983 versus their fixed historical F1 reference. Missing producer initialization digest and FP16-reference/ancestry limits remain explicit. Current-host native replay and the fixed precision diagnostic do not explain the larger previous H512 endpoint loss.

Warm-history preparation preserves a 211-input parent's function by zero-extending its input weights and retaining its normalization prefix, with an optional fitting-only estimator for appended statistics. Twelve focused tests and static checks pass on root and publication sources. Broader root compatibility checks passed eighteen tests and exposed one existing evaluation-class monkeypatch failure, recorded without claiming a blanket pass. Actual-parent parity and strong fits remain pending; the historical optional output-head compatibility path needs a narrow restoration. Active history also needs native serving support before release.

The corrected 52-target future-dynamics implementation passed numerical, causality and head-removal tests. Its hot throughput profile is running; the four-fit panel remains conditional on the inclusive three-hour ceiling. One local GPU worker, two aggregate CPU cores, 5 GB aggregate RAM/VRAM, no task swap, physical-disk scratch and strict FP32 remain binding. The i1 stage charged 4.249 hours including profiles, a preserved early failed launcher, exports and grading.

Evidence, failed attempts, hypothesis progression and exact artifacts are indexed in `research/campaign_2026-10-21/next_cycle_r1/FRONTIER.md` and unified notes. Frozen historical recipes are preserved. Generated tree snapshots remain stale while telemetry changes; strict freshness is not claimed. No stronger complete submission or public gain is established, and no competition upload is part of this draft.

## CPU delivery for the fixed i1 mixture — 23 October

Adds native causal-history inference for the 367-input i1 checkpoints, including checkpoint-owned scale priors, post-normalization masks, sequence resets and updates on every callback. Fixed 90%B/10%C epoch2 FP32 pairs are packaged separately for F0/seed1001 and F2/seed1002; no four-model blend or coefficient search.

The new build/packaging commands bind exact checkpoint hashes and provenance, native source/library hashes, Linux x86-64 ABI and the compressed ZIP limit. The official Rust Docker stage also removes the old curl-pipeline failure that could silently leave the compiler absent.

Validation: all three Linux x86-64 variants compiled for CPython3.11 abi3; static ELF checks passed (maximum GLIBC2.34, no libpython linkage); Ruff passed for all six changed Python files. Independent source review found no remaining concrete checkpoint-contract blocker. No local tests, inference, benchmarks or training were run.

The user explicitly requested continuing without the unavailable weights. A 1,613,069-byte library handoff archive was built; it contains no model weights and is not uploadable as a competition submission. The model ZIP, exact-output parity and one-CPU timing remain pending. No competition upload occurred.

[CPU packet, frozen candidates, receipts and receiving-host commands](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/dca42266/research/campaign_2026-10-21/next_cycle_r1/i1/submission_r1/README.md). The same note records the live23October portal snapshot:102 submissions, none today; latest two-parent0.66771, H5120.66667, team bestTL3 0.66832. These public scores do not measure the i1 mixture.
